key_insight: A deep-learning reconstructed whole-body DWI protocol cut scan time by 37% while preserving image quality and ADC measurements in metastatic prostate cancer.
clinical_relevance: This suggests a faster MRI option for staging and treatment assessment of metastatic prostate cancer without obvious loss of quantitative reliability.
method: Prospective single-centre study at 1.5T with two patient cohorts.
Compared standard WB-DWI with an accelerated DL-reconstructed WB-DWI protocol.
Used blinded radiologist image-quality scoring and lesion ADC comparison with statistical agreement testing.
evidence_signal: In 10 patients, image quality was rated across four anatomical stations; in 20 patients, lesion ADCs showed no significant difference between standard and accelerated protocols, with Bland-Altman analysis used to assess agreement.
watch_item: Single-centre cohorts were small, so broader validation is still needed before routine implementation.
paper_title: Evaluation of accelerated whole-body diffusion weighted imaging with deep learning reconstruction in patients with metastatic prostate cancer: assessment of image quality and ADC estimates.
